question_text: How many person records are in the 2024 ACS 1-year PUMS person file for Texas (psam_p48.csv)? Give the unweighted record count (number of rows). Answer format: integer, no separators.
How many person records in psam_p48.csv have AGEP (age) greater than or equal to 65? Give the unweighted record count. Answer format: integer, no separators.
How many records in the 2024 ACS 1-year PUMS household file for Texas (psam_h48.csv) have TYPEHUGQ equal to 1 (housing unit)? Give the unweighted record count. Answer format: integer, no separators.
How many person records in psam_p48.csv have SEX equal to 2 (female)? Give the unweighted record count. Answer format: integer, no separators.

How many person records in psam_p48.csv have ESR (employment status recode) equal to 3, meaning unemployed? Count records whose ESR value is exactly 3; ESR is blank for persons under 16 years old, and blank records are not counted. Give the unweighted record count. Answer format: integer, no separators.

How many records in psam_h48.csv are vacant housing units, defined as TYPEHUGQ equal to 1 (housing unit) and NP equal to 0 (vacant unit)? Give the unweighted record count. Answer format: integer, no separators.
Using person weights (PWGTP), what is the estimated number of persons in Texas aged 65 or older? Sum PWGTP over person records with AGEP >= 65. Answer format: integer, no separators.

Using household weights (WGTP), what is the estimated number of renter-occupied households in Texas? The universe is occupied housing units (TYPEHUGQ equal to 1 and NP greater than or equal to 1) with TEN equal to 3 (rented). Sum WGTP over that universe. Answer format: integer, no separators.
What is the PWGTP-weighted mean age over all person records? Weighted mean = sum(AGEP * PWGTP) / sum(PWGTP). Round to exactly two decimal places. Answer format: decimal2.

Among civilian employed persons (ESR equal to 1 or 2), what is the PWGTP-weighted mean wage or salary income (WAGP) in ADJINC-adjusted dollars? Adjusted wage = WAGP * ADJINC / 1000000. Weighted mean = sum(adjusted wage * PWGTP) / sum(PWGTP) over the universe. Persons with WAGP equal to 0 are part of the universe and included in the mean. Round to the nearest whole dollar. Answer format: integer, no separators.

What is the PWGTP-weighted median age over all person records? The weighted median is the smallest value v such that the sum of PWGTP over records with AGEP <= v is at least half of the total sum of PWGTP. Answer format: integer, no separators.

Among civilian employed persons (ESR equal to 1 or 2) with WAGP greater than 0, what is the PWGTP-weighted median wage or salary income in ADJINC-adjusted dollars? First compute the weighted median of unadjusted WAGP over the universe: the smallest value v such that the sum of PWGTP over universe records with WAGP <= v is at least half of the total PWGTP of the universe. Then multiply that median by ADJINC / 1000000 and round to the nearest whole dollar. Answer format: integer, no separators.

What is the WGTP-weighted median household income (HINCP) in ADJINC-adjusted dollars among occupied housing units (TYPEHUGQ equal to 1 and NP greater than or equal to 1)? The weighted median is the smallest value v such that the cumulative sum of WGTP over universe records with HINCP <= v is at least half of the total WGTP of the universe. Multiply that median by ADJINC / 1000000 and round to the nearest whole dollar. Answer format: integer, no separators.

What is the PWGTP-weighted 75th percentile of age over all person records, defined as the smallest value v such that the sum of PWGTP over records with AGEP <= v is at least 75 percent of the total sum of PWGTP? Answer format: integer, no separators.

What is the WGTP-weighted mean household size among occupied housing units (TYPEHUGQ equal to 1 and NP greater than or equal to 1)? Household size is NP. Weighted mean = sum(NP * WGTP) / sum(WGTP) over the universe. Round to exactly two decimal places. Answer format: decimal2.

What percentage of the PWGTP-weighted Texas population is under 18 years old? Compute 100 * sum(PWGTP over records with AGEP < 18) / sum(PWGTP over all person records). Round to one decimal place. Answer format: percent1 (a number with one decimal place, no percent sign).

Among persons aged 25 or older, what percentage hold a bachelor's degree or higher, meaning SCHL greater than or equal to 21? Compute 100 * sum(PWGTP over records with AGEP >= 25 and SCHL >= 21) / sum(PWGTP over records with AGEP >= 25). Round to one decimal place. Answer format: percent1 (a number with one decimal place, no percent sign).

Using person weights (PWGTP), what is the estimated number of persons living in renter-occupied housing units? Join each person record to its household record on SERIALNO and keep persons whose household has TYPEHUGQ equal to 1, NP greater than or equal to 1, and TEN equal to 3 (rented). Sum PWGTP over those persons. Answer format: integer, no separators.

What is the PWGTP-weighted median of household income (HINCP) across persons living in occupied housing units, in ADJINC-adjusted dollars? Join persons to households on SERIALNO; the universe is persons whose household has TYPEHUGQ equal to 1 and NP greater than or equal to 1. Each person carries their household's HINCP. The weighted median is the smallest value v such that the sum of PWGTP over universe persons with HINCP <= v is at least half of the total PWGTP of the universe. Multiply that median by ADJINC / 1000000 and round to the nearest whole dollar. Note this is a person-weighted quantity and is not the same as the household-weighted median. Answer format: integer, no separators.

What is the PWGTP-weighted mean household size experienced by a person? Join persons to households on SERIALNO; the universe is persons whose household has TYPEHUGQ equal to 1 and NP greater than or equal to 1. Each person carries their household's NP. Weighted mean = sum(NP * PWGTP) / sum(PWGTP) over the universe. Round to exactly two decimal places. Note this is a person-weighted quantity and differs from the household-weighted mean household size. Answer format: decimal2.

Using household weights (WGTP), what is the estimated number of occupied housing units whose householder is female? The householder is the person record with SPORDER equal to 1 for that SERIALNO. The universe is households with TYPEHUGQ equal to 1 and NP greater than or equal to 1; keep those whose householder has SEX equal to 2, and sum the household's WGTP (count each household once, with its household weight). Answer format: integer, no separators.

What is the WGTP-weighted median age of householders of occupied housing units? The householder is the person record with SPORDER equal to 1 for that SERIALNO; use that person's AGEP as the household's value. The universe is households with TYPEHUGQ equal to 1 and NP greater than or equal to 1, weighted by WGTP. The weighted median is the smallest value v such that the cumulative sum of WGTP over universe households with householder AGEP <= v is at least half of the total WGTP of the universe. Answer format: integer, no separators.

Using household weights (WGTP), what is the estimated number of occupied housing units in which at least one member is aged 65 or older? The universe is households with TYPEHUGQ equal to 1 and NP greater than or equal to 1. A household qualifies if at least one person record with the same SERIALNO has AGEP >= 65. Sum WGTP over qualifying households, counting each household once. Answer format: integer, no separators.

Using person weights (PWGTP), what is the estimated number of persons living in group quarters? Join persons to household records on SERIALNO and keep persons whose record has TYPEHUGQ equal to 2 (institutional) or 3 (noninstitutional). Sum PWGTP over those persons. Answer format: integer, no separators.

Among persons living in occupied housing units, what percentage live in owner-occupied units? Join persons to households on SERIALNO. The denominator is the sum of PWGTP over persons whose household has TYPEHUGQ equal to 1 and NP greater than or equal to 1. The numerator is the sum of PWGTP over the subset whose household additionally has TEN equal to 1 or 2 (owned with a mortgage or owned free and clear). Compute 100 * numerator / denominator and round to one decimal place. Answer format: percent1 (a number with one decimal place, no percent sign).

Among occupied housing units whose householder is aged 65 or older, what is the WGTP-weighted median household income (HINCP) in ADJINC-adjusted dollars? The householder is the person record with SPORDER equal to 1 for that SERIALNO. The universe is households with TYPEHUGQ equal to 1, NP greater than or equal to 1, and householder AGEP >= 65, weighted by WGTP. The weighted median is the smallest value v such that the cumulative sum of WGTP over universe households with HINCP <= v is at least half of the total WGTP of the universe. Multiply that median by ADJINC / 1000000 and round to the nearest whole dollar. Answer format: integer, no separators.

What is the WGTP-weighted median gross rent (GRNTP) in ADJHSG-adjusted dollars? The universe is occupied housing units (TYPEHUGQ equal to 1 and NP greater than or equal to 1) with a non-blank GRNTP. The weighted median is the smallest value v such that the cumulative sum of WGTP over universe records with GRNTP <= v is at least half of the total WGTP of the universe. Gross rent is adjusted with the housing adjustment factor, not the income one: multiply the median by ADJHSG / 1000000 and round to the nearest whole dollar. Answer format: integer, no separators.

What is the WGTP-weighted median property value (VALP) in ADJHSG-adjusted dollars among owner-occupied housing units? The universe is occupied housing units (TYPEHUGQ equal to 1 and NP greater than or equal to 1) with TEN equal to 1 or 2 (owned with a mortgage or owned free and clear) and a non-blank VALP. The weighted median is the smallest value v such that the cumulative sum of WGTP over universe records with VALP <= v is at least half of the total WGTP of the universe. Multiply the median by ADJHSG / 1000000 and round to the nearest whole dollar. Answer format: integer, no separators.

Using the 2023 ACS 1-year PUMS Texas person file, what is the PWGTP-weighted median age over all person records? The weighted median is the smallest value v such that the sum of PWGTP over records with AGEP <= v is at least half of the total sum of PWGTP. Answer format: integer, no separators.

By how much did the PWGTP-weighted total population of Texas grow from the 2023 ACS 1-year PUMS to the 2024 ACS 1-year PUMS? Compute sum(PWGTP) over all person records in the 2024 file minus sum(PWGTP) over all person records in the 2023 file. Answer format: integer, no separators.

Using the 2023 ACS 1-year PUMS Texas household file, what is the WGTP-weighted median household income (HINCP) in ADJINC-adjusted dollars among occupied housing units (TYPEHUGQ equal to 1 and NP greater than or equal to 1)? Use the ADJINC value from the 2023 file — each PUMS release carries its own ADJINC. The weighted median is the smallest value v such that the cumulative sum of WGTP over universe records with HINCP <= v is at least half of the total WGTP of the universe. Multiply that median by the 2023 file's ADJINC / 1000000 and round to the nearest whole dollar. Answer format: integer, no separators.

By what percentage did the WGTP-weighted median ADJINC-adjusted household income among occupied housing units (TYPEHUGQ equal to 1 and NP greater than or equal to 1) change from the 2023 ACS 1-year PUMS to the 2024 ACS 1-year PUMS for Texas? For each year separately: compute the weighted median of HINCP over that year's universe (smallest value v such that cumulative WGTP for HINCP <= v is at least half the universe's total WGTP), then multiply by that year's own ADJINC / 1000000 — do not round these intermediate values. Then compute 100 * (adjusted median 2024 - adjusted median 2023) / adjusted median 2023 and round to one decimal place. Answer format: percent1 (a number with one decimal place, no percent sign; use a leading minus sign if negative).

By how much did the WGTP-weighted number of renter-occupied households in Texas change from the 2023 ACS 1-year PUMS to the 2024 ACS 1-year PUMS? For each year, sum WGTP over households with TYPEHUGQ equal to 1, NP greater than or equal to 1, and TEN equal to 3 (rented). Compute the 2024 total minus the 2023 total. Answer format: integer, no separators; use a leading minus sign if negative.

Using the 2024 files, what is the standard error of the PWGTP-weighted estimate of the number of persons aged 65 or older, computed with the successive difference replication formula from the PUMS Accuracy of the Data documentation? Let X = sum of PWGTP over person records with AGEP >= 65, and let X_r = sum of PWGTP<r> over the same records for each of the 80 replicate weights PWGTP1 through PWGTP80. Then SE = sqrt( (4/80) * sum over r of (X_r - X)^2 ). Replicate weights can be negative; use them exactly as stored. Round to the nearest whole number. Answer format: integer, no separators.

Using the 2024 files, what is the standard error of the WGTP-weighted estimate of the number of renter-occupied households (TYPEHUGQ equal to 1, NP greater than or equal to 1, TEN equal to 3), computed with the successive difference replication formula? Let X = sum of WGTP over the universe and X_r = sum of WGTP<r> over the same records for each of the 80 replicate weights WGTP1 through WGTP80. Then SE = sqrt( (4/80) * sum over r of (X_r - X)^2 ). Replicate weights can be negative; use them exactly as stored. Round to the nearest whole number. Answer format: integer, no separators.

Using the 2024 files, what is the standard error of the PWGTP-weighted mean wage or salary income in ADJINC-adjusted dollars among civilian employed persons (ESR equal to 1 or 2), computed with the successive difference replication formula? The full-sample estimate is X = sum(WAGP * ADJINC / 1000000 * PWGTP) / sum(PWGTP) over the universe, and each replicate estimate X_r recomputes the same ratio with PWGTP<r> in place of PWGTP in both numerator and denominator (r = 1..80). Then SE = sqrt( (4/80) * sum over r of (X_r - X)^2 ). Replicate weights can be negative; use them exactly as stored. Round to the nearest whole dollar. Answer format: integer, no separators.

Using the 2024 files, what is the standard error of the WGTP-weighted median household income (HINCP) in ADJINC-adjusted dollars among occupied housing units (TYPEHUGQ equal to 1 and NP greater than or equal to 1), computed with the successive difference replication formula? The full-sample estimate X is the weighted median of HINCP over the universe (smallest value v such that the cumulative sum of WGTP over universe records with HINCP <= v is at least half of the total WGTP of the universe) multiplied by ADJINC / 1000000, without rounding. Each replicate estimate X_r applies the identical median definition with WGTP<r> in place of WGTP (both in the cumulative sums and in the total), then multiplies by ADJINC / 1000000. Then SE = sqrt( (4/80) * sum over r of (X_r - X)^2 ). Replicate weights can be negative; use them exactly as stored. Round the final SE to the nearest whole dollar. Answer format: integer, no separators.

Using the 2024 files, what is the standard error, in percentage points, of the percentage of persons aged 25 or older holding a bachelor's degree or higher (SCHL greater than or equal to 21), computed with the successive difference replication formula? The full-sample estimate is X = 100 * sum(PWGTP over records with AGEP >= 25 and SCHL >= 21) / sum(PWGTP over records with AGEP >= 25), and each replicate estimate X_r recomputes the same ratio with PWGTP<r> in place of PWGTP in both numerator and denominator (r = 1..80). Then SE = sqrt( (4/80) * sum over r of (X_r - X)^2 ). Replicate weights can be negative; use them exactly as stored. Round to exactly two decimal places. Answer format: decimal2.
